name: vscode-assist
description: Navigation shortcuts VS Code does not ship, bound to keys VS Code does not use.

assist.keymap.enabled.markdownDescription:
The master switch for every key this extension binds. Every contributed keybinding carries `config.assist.keymap.enabled` in its `when` clause, so turning this off hands all of them back at once - the commands stay available from the Command Palette and from your own `keybindings.json`.

This exists because an extension has no way to release a key once it has taken it. `keybindings.json` can remove a rule with a leading `-`, and your rules always win over an extension's, but there is no equivalent an extension can ship. A `when` clause is the only lever on this side of the line, so the switch is built out of one.

assist.roundTrip.chain.markdownDescription:
Which language-server providers `Alt+G` asks, in order. The first one that answers with a location other than the one under the cursor wins - that is what makes the jump a round trip rather than a one-way trip. On a call site `definition` answers immediately; standing on the definition itself it can only point at where you already are, so the next link in the chain takes over and lands you on the declaration.

Drop `implementation` if your project is mostly free functions and the extra query is wasted. Add `typeDefinition` to fall through to the type of the symbol when nothing else answers.

assist.roundTrip.pickWhenAmbiguous.markdownDescription: When a provider answers with several locations - overloads, or a virtual with many overrides - show a picker. Turn this off to always take the first result and never be interrupted.
